lanes.from_chamber_title: What It Offers the Cutaway Reader

nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.heading: section
text: An archive can preserve every page and still be impossible to remember. The magazine mosaic keeps each photograph of each page, yet a reader who closes it retains almost nothing about where anything was.

Descent solved a harder problem. Its mines have no reliable floor or ceiling, and players still learned them, because memory attached to topology and action together: the broad chamber with the vertical shaft that leads back toward the blue door.

nodes.title: Preliminaries and Notation
nodes.heading: section
text: A work is a set of units. Each section is a chamber with a stable identifier, each subsection an alcove, and each reference a passage.
The semantic graph records meaning. The spatial ledger records remembered location. A reader log records what one person actually did.

nodes.title: Chambers
nodes.heading: subsection
text: A chamber keeps its identifier and coordinates for the life of the work. Revision may enlarge it or seal it, never move it.

nodes.title: Passages
nodes.heading: subsection
text: A passage is physically two-way. The citation it realizes keeps its direction in the graph.

nodes.title: The Cutaway Map
nodes.heading: section
text: Using the notation of Section [sec:prelim], the automap removes texture, lighting and surface detail so that connectivity is all that remains.

It opens in the viewer's current orientation, centred on the present chamber, and discloses only what has been visited or revealed. Traversed passages are white; revealed ones are a faint blue envelope; the rest is absent.

nodes.title: Route Persistence
nodes.heading: section
text: A Stars! repeat route becomes a reproducible flight path. Cruise flies it with the same translations and rotations a pilot would make, and any key takes control back.

nodes.title: Supervisory Memory
nodes.heading: section

threads.text: needs a recall study with returning readers

text: Orientation comes from invariants amid transformation, see [sub:chambers]. The reader may roll upside down and approach a chamber along another axis, but its connections stay where they were.

A second loop sits above the first. Routes declared in the strategic view are flown as real trajectories in the mine, and the log of what happened lets a reader return after days and resume where the argument was left. Policies extend this. A route can be declared once as a rule, such as prerequisites before dependents, and recomputed whenever the source or the reader's history changes, so the plan stays current without being redrawn by hand.

nodes.title: Objections from Search
nodes.heading: section

threads.text: whether instant retrieval erodes place memory is deliberately left open

text: Search reaches any point instantly, which is exactly why it produces no place memory. Retrieval answers where a phrase is; it says nothing about what surrounds it or how one arrived, contra [sec:thesis].

nodes.title: Applications to an Essay Corpus
nodes.heading: section
text: Six hundred works become six hundred small levels, each generated from its own source, each learnable with the same axis rule. Illustrations hang on the far wall of the chamber they open.

nodes.title: Closing
nodes.heading: section
text: The test for the whole design is simple. After closing it for a day, can the reader say where an argument was, how they reached it, and which passage they meant to explore next?

nodes.title: Formal Model
nodes.heading: section
text: Ledger invariants, per [sec:prelim]: identifiers are never reused, coordinates are never recomputed, and withdrawn chambers remain as sealed volumes.

nodes.title: Control Table
nodes.heading: section
text: Left hand translates: W and S surge, A and D strafe, R and F heave, Q and E roll. Right hand orients: H and L yaw, J and K pitch. Tab or semicolon opens the automap.

nodes.title: A Deceptively Simple System
nodes.heading: section
text: Mackenzie presents Lotus Notes as a way to build distributed document collections without commissioning a database application. An ordinary user sees forms, folders, views and documents. Beneath them sit replication, access control, application logic and conflict handling among computers that are only intermittently connected.

nodes.title: What a Document Was
nodes.heading: section
text: A Notes document is a self-describing record of indeterminate size. It can hold text and numbers, rich text, images, sound, spreadsheets, embedded files and links to other notes. A database carries these records together with the forms that display them, the views that sort them and the permissions that govern them, so the records and their interface travel together.

nodes.title: Replication Without a Master
nodes.heading: section

threads.text: compare conflict handling with later offline-first systems in detail

text: A Notes database can have many replicas and none of them is the master. Servers synchronise over a network and a laptop can dial in from a hotel. When two people edit the same note independently, Notes keeps both versions and marks the conflict for a person to resolve, much as offline-first systems do today.
Deletions travel too. A replica passes on a notice that a note was removed, so absence is recorded rather than inferred.

nodes.title: Files Inside Records
nodes.heading: section
text: A conventional file can be linked from where it lives, attached as a copy, or embedded as an object that opens in its own application and writes itself back. Linking breaks across intermittently connected machines; attachment is portable but awkward to edit; embedding is smoother. Field exchange can keep a title in a word-processing file and the title shown in a view in step.

nodes.title: Limits the Article Admits
nodes.heading: section
text: Notes is not relational. Data is duplicated between notes, and keeping it consistent needs agents or an SQL server. Notes 3 cannot search inside attachments, so repositories need abstracts and metadata beside the file icons. It has no distributed locking.

nodes.title: Two Working Repositories
nodes.heading: section
text: S. G. Warburg kept reusable paragraphs, charts and finished presentations in a shared repository. Coopers & Lybrand ran audits through Notes, with distributed teams sharing templates, plans, outstanding issues and completed work. In both cases the repository is where the work is done, not where it is filed afterwards.

nodes.title: Comparison with GitHub
nodes.heading: section
text: GitHub is organised around version-controlled files, commits and branches. Notes was organised around semistructured records, replicated applications, forms and views. Both version, distribute and permit collaboration, but Notes stores the interface with the information while Git stores a history of file states.

nodes.title: What It Offers the Cutaway Reader
nodes.heading: section
text: A work in the Cutaway Reader is already closer to a Notes database than to a directory: prose, illustrations, relations, routes and a reader history travel together, as in [sec:notes-record]. The difference is that Notes presents its records through lists and forms, while the Cutaway Reader adds a stable geography as another view of the same records.

L:sec:notes-cutaway.title: What It Offers the Cutaway Reader

nodes.title: A Long Convergence
nodes.heading: section
text: The idea of flying through a body of writing did not arrive at once. It gathered over several projects, each contributing one piece, until a concrete object could hold them together.

nodes.title: Haplopraxis
nodes.heading: section
text: The earliest form joined Stars!, Descent, typing drills and simulation in a single game. Stars! supplied colonies, research, trade routes and processes that ran unattended; Descent supplied embodied exploration. Even then the large persistent system was kept distinct from local action.

nodes.title: Polyxan and Semantic Space
nodes.heading: section
text: Polyxan moved the subject from games to knowledge: papers, simulations and essays with provenance, typed links and versioning that does not depend on files. Later notes projected embeddings into a navigable starspace with finite travel times and a local frame for each reader.

nodes.title: Navigation as Reasoning
nodes.heading: section
text: Descent gives a pilot three translations and three rotations, and the pilot never computes a route. Simple local controls accumulate into whatever trajectory the task needs. The trajectory essays generalised this: inference is navigation, not lookup, and concepts are reached by shortened paths.

nodes.title: Two Loops
nodes.heading: section
text: The automap is a second perception-and-control loop. The first is local: wall, doorway, corridor. The second is topological: cycles, escape routes and shortcuts. A mine is remembered as a graph, not as a list of directions, see [sec:games-trajectories].

nodes.title: Repeat Routes and Policies
nodes.heading: section
text: Stars! freighters on fixed routes, patrol limits and aggression settings describe a progression from direct control to repeatable routes, to bounded policies, to trusting the infrastructure while turns advance. Cruise in the reader is the second step; route policies are the third.

nodes.title: What Was New
nodes.heading: section

threads.text: trace the Plenum Ascent prototype as a separate lineage

text: The generator was new: one level per essay, sections as chambers, references as tunnels, appendices as shafts, and fixed axes shared by every level. So were the reassigned verbs and the rule that revision may enlarge a mine but never rearrange it.

nodes.title: Where Descent's Map Succeeds
nodes.heading: section
text: In the simpler levels the wireframe gives an immediate topology: a central chamber, branches, a few loops, recognisable ends. In the dense late levels, drawing every edge at once becomes a thicket. The map stays usable there only because the pilot has already learned the space by moving through it.

nodes.title: Egocentric Before Exhaustive
nodes.heading: section
text: The map should open in the reader's current orientation, centred on the present chamber, with the route just travelled highlighted and remote geometry dimmed. A local map with seven recognisable connections is easier to use than a truthful picture of a whole corpus.

nodes.title: Sparse, Invariant Colour
nodes.heading: section
text: White carries the skeleton. Colour marks what a reader can act on: the current route, exits to other works, prerequisite doors, open threads, beacons and the present chamber. Illustrations appear on the map only as simple landmark glyphs.

nodes.title: Three States of Discovery
nodes.heading: section

threads.text: whether revealed structure should ever fade again is left open

text: Unexplored structure is absent. Revealed but unvisited structure is a faint envelope. Traversed passages are solid. A brief scan may show more for a moment, but only being there makes it permanent.

nodes.title: Semantic Depth
nodes.heading: section
text: Viewing distance should change the representation, not only its size. Close in, the map shows the current section and its alcoves; further out, the part; further still, the whole work; beyond that, the work becomes one system among others. Geometry belongs only at the scale where it affects the next decision.
